Done. Only `amap.py` changed.

Root cause
`amap.py:3` did `[await fn(x) for x in items]` — fully sequential. It never ran anything concurrently, ignored `limit` entirely, never validated it, and would eagerly `await` every item.

Fix (`amap.py`)
A lazy sliding-window scheduler:
- Validates `limit < 1` up front → raises `ValueError`.
- Primes at most `limit` tasks, then awaits the oldest and schedules one new item per completion. At most `limit` invocations are ever in flight and at most `limit` tasks exist ahead of consumption — so a 10^9-element or infinite generator never spawns unbounded tasks.
- A `deque` keeps tasks in input order, so results come back in input order regardless of completion timing.
- An `asyncio.Semaphore(limit)` guards each invocation as a second cap.
- A `finally` block cancels and gathers surviving tasks on error/cancellation, so failed runs don't leak running tasks or emit "exception never retrieved" warnings.
- Supports any sync iterable (list/tuple/range/set/dict/str/generator) plus async iterables, pulled lazily.

Verification (all real runs)
- `python test_public.py` → `PUBLIC_OK`.
- Extra suite (`/tmp/check_amap.py`) passed under `-W error::RuntimeWarning`:
  - order/values correct with reversed delays; `limit` 0/-1/-5 all raise `ValueError`
  - a concurrency probe observing peak in-flight hits exactly 4 with `limit=4` (proves real concurrency) and never exceeds it
  - generator/range/tuple/set/dict/str/async-generator inputs, empty input
  - lazy generator: only the bounded window is pulled from a 10^9 sequence
  - exception propagation with no orphan tasks; outer-task cancellation cleans up

Public API `bounded_map(fn, items, limit)` is unchanged. Extra checks live in `/tmp`, not the repo; working tree shows only `M amap.py`.
